note: Taste receptor neuron (GRN) firing-rate models, spikes/s, used by scripts/fly_taste.gd. Values are literature RANGES turned into simple saturating curves; basis: approximate (edit freely). Concentrations in mM; osmolarity approximated as sucrose + 2*NaCl + bitter.

sources.sugar: Labellar L-type sugar GRNs fire tens of spikes/s to 100 mM sucrose, saturating near 1 M (Hiroi et al. 2002 Chem Senses; Dahanukar et al. 2007 Neuron).
sources.water: Water GRNs (ppk28) fire ~20-40 spikes/s to pure water and are suppressed by rising osmolarity (Cameron et al. 2010 PNAS; Chen et al. 2010).
sources.low_salt: Low NaCl (<=100 mM) excites sugar/low-salt GRNs (Zhang et al. 2013 Science; Jaeger et al. 2018 eLife).
sources.high_salt: High NaCl (>=250 mM) excites high-salt GRNs (Zhang et al. 2013; Jaeger et al. 2018).
sources.bitter: Bitter GRNs fire tens of spikes/s to mM caffeine / sub-mM denatonium (Weiss et al. 2011 Neuron; Meunier et al. 2003).
sources.glutamate: Glutamate-sensing GRNs (LB1e); no glutamate in the arena yet.
